chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman from Hammad from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whatever befalls the servant while he is in the state of ihram during his ihram, it is upon the master, if he permitted him to enter into ihram."

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.مُحْرِم: One who is in the state of ihram

ai.seo_question: Who bears the penalty if a servant violates ihram rules during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of vicarious financial liability (kaffarah) in Hajj jurisprudence, establishing that the master assumes the penalty for violations committed by his servant acting under his explicit permission. This ruling is particularly significant in the context of classical Islamic society where servants often performed Hajj on behalf of their masters, highlighting the legal distinction between the agent's action and the principal's financial responsibility. It serves as a foundational text in the chapter on expiation for unintentional or conditional violations during the state of ihram.
